notes: PILOT: time segmentation, short training window. Stack on the base: python -m dskit.pipeline workflow configs/workflow.json --args configs/pilot-base.json --args configs/pilot-window-250.json. Every fold trains on the last 250 dates instead of 450 (about one year): it adapts faster to a new regime and estimates with less data. The GRU's edge over the MLP shrank from 58.9% on the full history to 3.0% after 2019, so the data are not stationary; this asks whether recency beats sample size. Each window pilot changes three things at once: the training window, the warm-up years steps 4-6 select on (the fold grid is end-anchored), and the window of every reference, including horizon_empirical, the skill denominator. Skill against the references inside one run therefore does NOT answer recency against sample size. Compare RAW CRPS on the dates every window run scores (the 750 run's scored set is nested inside the 450 and 250 sets): read {work_dir}/step6/study_QQQ/evaluate/later/scores.parquet from pilot-base and both window runs, keep the common (quote_date, expiry) rows, and the raw variant only (scores carry a raw and a calibrated row per model), and compare each model's mean crps there. The six references have fixed specs, so they answer the window question cleanly; the step-6 candidate is selected on different warm-up years in each run, so its gap is directional only. The shared set is small (the 750 run's scored folds, roughly 160 dates on the earlier QQQ cohort) and has no interval: treat it as a screen. Pair it with pilot-window-750.json.
